title: Colorway Editor Updates | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to Colorways in CLO 2025.0 allows you to easily toggle the Colorway Editor with a keyboard shortcut and quickly edit the current colorway by clicking color chips in the Object Browser. You can also edit the fabric's side and back, along with trims, directly in the Colorway Editor. Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Chapters: 
00:00 - Introduction
00:18 Object Browser Color Chips 
00:53 Colorway Shortcut 
01:20 Fabric Back and front in Colorway Editor

summary: ```markdown # Colorway Editor Updates | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive Hey everyone, it's Phoebe, and I have some great updates to share with you for Colorway with our 2025.0 release. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Switching Between Colorways One cool thing with our Colorway is that now, if you're working in your simulation mode, you can switch between your Colorways without having to go into the Colorway interface. That's right! You can just use these color chips, select them, and it will automatically update to that Colorway for you. Pretty cool, right? ## Accessing Colorway If you still want to open up Colorway, there's an easier way now. There's a shortcut for 'O'. Just as a reminder, if you need to know where Colorway is located, it's in your top toolbar right underneath Production. You can go to Production, then Colorway, and there you'll even see the shortcut. ## Exploring Colorways I’m going to use the shortcut 'O' to open Colorway. Here, I have my Colorways, and I can go through them. You might notice something really interesting: you have both front and back Colorways. If you look at the increases, you’ll see these are not in the эконом section. You only have one or two of the increases, and on top of that, you have one or two extra grids. You can screenshot them with your humbuck into Colorway, making it easy to edit those out. That would be great! It will console you, but it also enables you to visualize some of the changes. ## Editing Colorways This feature allows you to create some fine silhouettes for your ordered pieces. If I’d like, I could go into here and edit and adjust. I'm going to select this and pick a slightly darker color to apply and close. For this one, I think the light works, but for another, maybe I want a brighter yellow. I could go in, click this, and choose a bright yellow, apply it, and switch. I’ll also make sure to adjust this here to a bright yellow. Now you can see how the back of my fabric has been adjusted for both my black and yellow Colorways. ## Back Textures and Trims For all my other Colorways, you can see that some additional adjustments have not been made yet between the black and yellow Colorways regarding different front and back textures. This adjustment will also happen for trims. If you have multiple sections of trims, you can see all of those laid out in your Colorway editor. You can edit and adjust them while going through the options. I even have the puller and slider separated out, so I could select my slider, adjust that, and then select my puller to adjust as well. All of these can be adjusted within Colorway, allowing for quick and easy selection. ## Conclusion If you have any questions, first off, thank you for watching the video! If you have any questions, check that comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe! Keep having fun in Clo, and really check out that YouTube channel—there are so many great videos for you to learn from. Thanks so much! ```
